author: ZILIAN
quote: I went into GTA6 with pretty high expectations, and honestly, by the end most of that enthusiasm was gone.What bothered me most was how much the freedom shrinks. Take Jason's early-game section: step outside his house and there are cars you can't steal, pedestrians you can't touch. That's a far cry from the GTA I know — an open world where you can do whatever you want. For me, that constant feeling of being hemmed in stings more than any **** mission design didn't win me over either. In the footage, characters clip through each other and hit detection goes haywire, and a lot of scenes lean on QTEs and scripted sequences that leave almost no room to improvise. Melee combat boils down to "mash a few buttons and it's over," and some of the enemies in gunfights are so inaccurate they're not a threat at all. I even saw flying a plane into a building and getting no reaction whatsoever — the physics feel unfinished.What confused me even more was where all the attention went. Jason and Lucia's romance, plus decorating the house, cooking, dates, gift-giving — it takes up way too much space, and the protagonist ends up feeling passive. I don't play GTA to manage a relationship and do chores; it feels like the game is being pushed into being a dating sim / household **** save system didn't do me any favors either. Apparently you can't make multiple manual saves, which means every choice I make is locked in for the ending, with no way to jump back to an earlier point and try something else the way you can in GTA V or Red Dead Redemption 2. If you like experimenting with different choices, that's a real **** seeing the media mostly shower it with praise only made me more skeptical. Given everything I saw, I just can't get behind those scores.
